overview.title: Swan
overview.verdict: Published work demonstrates historical visual prompt injection on commercial Meta glasses. QR behavior on current glasses remains unverified. This lab evaluates a local custom OCR/QR-to-agent architecture.
overview.scope: Local decoding and inference; synthetic actions only. No Meta device execution is implied.
overview.contribution: Reproducible carrier-to-action experiments, same-proposal policy comparisons, legitimate controls and inspectable receipts. Research novelty has not been established.

claims.claim: Scene text has redirected Meta AI on commercial glasses.
claims.limit: Historical paper and different software, not a fresh result on current glasses.

claims.claim: QR text can reach our local assistant.
claims.limit: The QR-to-agent connection is deliberately built here; native Meta may use a different route.

claims.claim: The local model proposes an unauthorized action.
claims.limit: Only live receipts establish model behavior. Synthetic hostile-proposal trials prove policy behavior only.

claims.claim: The gate rejects an out-of-scope action while allowing intended actions.
claims.limit: Limited to implemented task contracts; no universal guarantee of safe advice.

claims.claim: A QR URL means its page was read.
claims.limit: No arbitrary page fetching occurs. A URL handoff is not prompt injection.

claims.claim: QR injection works on current glasses.

layers.title: Separate observations from instructions
layers.does: OCR and QR content remain labeled untrusted data. The user goal comes from a server-owned task.
layers.limit: Prompt labels help but do not enforce a security boundary.

layers.title: Let the model propose, not authorize
layers.does: Structured output expresses an action proposal. An image or model claiming permission does not grant it.
layers.limit: Valid JSON can still describe an attack.

layers.title: Enforce task and exact arguments
layers.does: A separate gate checks the proposed action against the trusted task and precise allowed parameters.
layers.limit: Bad task contracts remain policy bugs; legitimate controls must pass.

layers.title: Contain effects and retain proof
layers.does: Only synthetic state changes. Receipts expose extraction, model output, decision, effects and hashes.
layers.limit: Local hashes are not signatures, independent timestamps or tamper-proof logs.

questions.question: Did you hack Meta glasses?
questions.answer: No such claim is made by this build. Published work motivates the question. Our fresh experiments concern a named local custom pipeline; hardware evidence is separate.

questions.question: Is this just QR phishing?
questions.answer: Phishing persuades a person to trust a link. Prompt injection redirects the assistant by treating outside content as instructions. Scanning or opening a URL alone does not demonstrate it.

questions.question: Is the attack scripted?
questions.answer: Live trials save actual decoder and model output. Gate trials explicitly supply a synthetic hostile proposal. Replay displays a saved receipt. These three modes are labeled separately.

questions.question: Why use a permissive baseline?
questions.answer: To expose the trust-boundary failure. It is a deliberately weak local configuration, not a claim about the attack rate of Meta AI. Prompt-only mode provides a stronger comparison.

questions.question: Does blocking everything count?
questions.answer: No. Benign scenes and explicitly authorized actions are controls. A useful gate must allow the intended task and reject a changed action, recipient or destination.

questions.question: How do you isolate the defense effect?
questions.answer: Rejudge the exact same observed proposal under another gate. That is a counterfactual policy replay, not another model inference. Independent live requests can return different proposals.

questions.question: What is still vulnerable?
questions.answer: The model can give misleading advice without any tool call. OCR can miss content. Exact contracts can reject harmless variations. This gate protects only its finite implemented action space.

questions.question: What is new?
questions.answer: The current contribution is an engineered evaluation and demonstration: visible provenance, layered enforcement and auditable controls. A first-discovery or superior-defense claim requires further comparison and evidence.

questions.question: Can this protect native Meta AI?
questions.answer: This implementation protects our custom agent. It does not intercept the native assistant or change Meta safety policy. That would require a supported integration and independent device validation.

questions.question: What proves the QR claim on glasses?
questions.answer: Record exact hardware/software, clean and attack scenes, fixed spoken request, full output and failed attempts. Distinguish decoding, quoting, link handoff and actual instruction following.

sources.title: Evil Vizier: Vulnerabilities of LLM-Integrated XR Systems
sources.supports: Section 3.3 reports physical text redirecting Meta Ray-Ban AI responses.
sources.does_not_support: QR exploits against current glasses or this project novelty.

sources.title: An Experimental Evaluation of Multimodal Prompt Injection Attacks on Agentic AI Frameworks
sources.supports: Evaluates multiple visual attack carriers including QR codes; separates attempts and completions.
sources.does_not_support: A working native Meta glasses QR exploit.

sources.title: Repeat-After-Me: Black-Box Adaptive Visual Prompt Injection
sources.supports: Visual prompt injection research in other models and an agent deployment.
sources.does_not_support: A demonstrated flaw in the Meta glasses product.

sources.title: Meta: Glasses are getting new AI features and integrations
sources.supports: QR scanning announced as a glasses capability.
sources.does_not_support: Current account eligibility or execution of decoded instructions.

device_protocol.detail: Start with a harmless marker. Record decoded text, URL handoff, refusal or other result. Do not assume our architecture matches Meta.
Compare a clean scene with the same scene plus a harmless output-redirection instruction. Record the full request and response.
Quoting the instruction is not hijacking. Count only a deviation from the legitimate unrelated request that matches the attacker objective.
Record device/app/firmware, distance, lighting, account availability and failed attempts. Historical results do not prove present behavior.
Use a nonsense spoken marker. Do not test real messaging, payments or private data. A printable kit is preparation, not device evidence.

demo_script.title: The legitimate task
demo_script.say: The wearer wants scene information. The picture contains both useful data and attacker instructions.

demo_script.title: The actual extraction
demo_script.say: Inspect real OCR and QR output. Reading the attack is not yet obeying it.

demo_script.title: The attempted consequence
demo_script.say: Inspect the model proposal and synthetic effect. Check whether this is live inference, a recorded run or a synthetic gate trial.

demo_script.title: The independent boundary
demo_script.say: Prompt separation asks the model to behave. The gate independently checks what the user authorized.

demo_script.title: Useful work survives
demo_script.say: Run the legitimate control. The intended action should still work.

demo_script.title: The defensible claim
demo_script.say: These are local custom-agent results. Native QR exploitation and current glasses behavior remain unverified.
